title: Redwood discovery: model selection - Therma Analytics
summary: Initial model-selection discovery for Therma Analytics evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for multilingual thermal-analysis assistant. Main concerns: context length for long reports, tool-calling for internal data fetches, multilingual accuracy (EN/ES/FR), latency vs cost, and security (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed next steps: share benchmark guidance, pricing for dedicated options, security pack (SOC2 + VPC/on-prem runbook), and schedule pilot benchmark with 8k/32k context tests.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-11-02 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (CTO - Therma), Elena Gomez (ML Eng), Sophie Martin (PM)

Summary section (auto-gen, may be rough): quick discovery about model choices for a multilingual, long-context assistant that can call internal tools/APIs for retrieving sensor reports.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Liam from our Solutions Eng team. how are you all?
[00:07] Ravi Patel: hey Maya, thanks. doing good. we're excited to dig in, we've been evaluating a couple of open models and wondering where Redwood fits.
[00:12] Liam O'Neill: great — quick agenda, would like to understand your current infra, target latency, cost constraints, languages, and tool-calling patterns, then we can map models and deployment modes.
[00:22] Sophie Martin: sounds good. we have lunchtime constraints so we'll try to be concise.
[00:26] Elena Gomez: quick note — we will ask about support for 32k context windows and some fine-tuning / retrieval patterns.

[02:05] Ravi Patel: overview: Therma's product analyzes thermal imagery & sensor logs and generates reports. users upload hours-long sessions, typical prompt+context ends up around 6k-12k tokens. for some customers, they want full-session transcripts up to 30k tokens.
[02:22] Maya Chen: good to know. so you have both mid-length (6-12k) and occasional long (25-30k). are those full fidelity or can you summarize before sending to model?
[02:30] Sophie Martin: customers expect near-raw detail for audits so we can't aggressively summarize prior to LLM, sometimes we chunk but prefer single-shot when possible.
[03:01] Liam O'Neill: that pushes us toward models that support 32k contexts or an approach with clever retrieval + KV cache. for hosted, we have verified model variants with 32k; for Dedicated and Private you can also pin custom model builds.

[04:15] Elena Gomez: model-wise we've been looking at LLaMA derivatives, Mistral, and a couple of MPT forks. where do you typically land for accuracy multilingual? we need EN/ES/FR primary.
[04:30] Maya Chen: LLM landscape is noisy. in general: LLaMA-derivs (7B-70B) vary; Mistral 7B/8x mixes do well in some bench marks, but for long context you want models trained/optimized for extended context or we apply Redwood's compilation & kernel selection to improve perf. we also test Claude-like and Anthropic in-house for comparison, and community models on HF.
[04:58] Ravi Patel: when you say "Redwood's compilation" — can you explain?
[05:05] Liam O'Neill: sure — the runtime picks optimized kernels depending on model architecture and seq length distribution, and we do KV cache management plus continuous batching to keep latency predictable. for large context we also do prefix caching to avoid recomputing tokens. transcription note: liam said "KV cahce" earlier in the doc, sorry.

[06:40] Sophie Martin: for tool-calling — our flows invoke internal retrieval APIs (compliance docs, sensor raw blobs). we need function/tool calls with structured responses so the app can route to downstream services. is that supported?
[06:55] Maya Chen: yes — Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured output. on Hosted API it's available today; for Dedicated/Private you can map network routes to customer APIs (VPC peering or private link).

[08:10] Elena Gomez: any gotchas for security? we need SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and KMS/HSM for key control.
[08:22] Maya Chen: covered — hosted is SOC2-backed, we offer SAML SSO, RBAC + audit logs. Dedicated adds dedicated GPU pools and optional customer-managed KMS; Private gives you full on-prem control and HSM integrations. we'll share the security pack after the call.

[09:40] Ravi Patel: latency targets: for interactive UIs we need 300-600ms per response (for small prompt tasks) and up to 2s for longer generations. is that realistic with 32k context?
[09:55] Liam O'Neill: 300-600ms is tough for long contexts; for 32k full-generation latency will be higher — often in the 1.5-4s range depending on model size and batch. Dedicated GPUs with pinned capacity get you predictable tail latencies. Hosted SLOs depend on plan, but we route and fallback to smaller variants if needed.

[11:12] Sophie Martin: cost — our finance wants unit economics. do you recommend hosted first then dedicated?
[11:20] Maya Chen: common path: hosted for PoC and early usage, then Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput and better unit cost. Private is chosen for strict compliance. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization, batching, and model variant to reduce token cost.

[12:30] Elena Gomez: Felipe, I mean liam, sorry — do you run your own benchmarks? we have a specific eval set (multilingual medical/thermal terms). can Redwood run that on a few models?
[12:45] Liam O'Neill: yes, we can run evals. typical bench: latency, throughput, token cost, and quality on your eval set. suggest we run 8k and 32k contexts across 3 model families (LLaMA-70B-32K quantized, MistralX-like 32k, and a tuned Falcon/MPT variant).

[14:04] Ravi Patel: are there managed model variants you provide or do we bring our own?
[14:11] Maya Chen: both. we have a model catalog of curated open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles. you can also bring private models to Dedicated/Private. for hosted we can onboard some custom weights with an enterprise process.

[15:20] Sophie Martin: multilingual: which models usually perform best for ES/FR?
[15:26] Liam O'Neill: big picture: Open models with diverse pretraining (LLaMA-derivs with additional multilingual corpora) and some Mistral variants show strong EN/ES/FR. We run task-specific evals because micro performance depends on your domain vocabulary (thermal terms).

[16:50] Elena Gomez: retrieval patterns: do you recommend chunking + RAG or longer single-shot with 32k?
[16:58] Liam O'Neill: tradeoff: single-shot simplifies prompt engineering but costs more and increases latency. RAG + tool calls with retrieval and a compact summary often hits a sweet spot for cost/latency; for audit-level needs we can do hybrid — retrieve the chunk for the specific question and then provide full-session transcript to the model for certain gated workflows.

[18:35] Ravi Patel: about function calls — can we do deterministic structured outputs (JSON schema) for downstream pipes?
[18:42] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood supports structured output enforcement and function calling; we can surface model-level guides and output validators. if you need guaranteed schema adherence we recommend a small post-processor step to validate outputs.

[20:00] Sophie Martin: are there examples of customers that moved from hosted to Dedicated for cost reasons?
[20:08] Maya Chen: multiple — engineering-heavy apps that reached steady usage. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, autoscaling policies and better unit pricing. we'll include a case note in the follow-up.

[21:30] Elena Gomez: questions on quantization — how much accuracy hit do you see with int8/int4 on these long-context workloads?
[21:40] Liam O'Neill: quantization trade-offs vary by model; many modern models tolerate int8 with negligible quality loss for generation; int4 can be fine for some workloads but you may see regressions on rare token predictions. Redwood Optimize runs model + workload-specific recommendations. we'll run cand tests with your eval set.

[23:05] Ravi Patel: legal/procurement question: what does private on-prem pricing look like vs Dedicated reserved?
[23:13] Maya Chen: private on-prem typically has a platform fee + support/implementation; Dedicated is reserved capacity commitment monthly/annual. I'll get finance to send a template pricing sheet for both — pricing varies by commit and support tier.

[25:00] Sophie Martin: timeline: we want to pick a vendor within 6-8 weeks and run a 4-week pilot. is that feasible?
[25:08] Maya Chen: yes, hosted PoC can start within days; Dedicated pilot provisioning takes 1-2 weeks for capacity, Private on-prem is longer depending on install.

[26:20] Elena Gomez: network stuff — VPC peering / private link? how does data egress work?
[26:28] Liam O'Neill: Hosted supports private link options, Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer-managed egress. Private on-prem keeps data within your network. for logging we can stream audit logs to your SIEM.

[28:00] Ravi Patel: okay next steps — can you run 8k/32k benchmarks on our eval set and propose recommended model variants?
[28:09] Maya Chen: absolutely, we can run those. we'll need your eval dataset and a short benchmark rubric. we'll run on three candidate models and send a report with latency, quality scores, and cost estimates.

[29:40] Sophie Martin: and security docs?
[29:45] Maya Chen: yes, we'll attach SOC2 report, SAML integration guide, VPC/private runbook, and KMS/HSM integration notes.

[31:00] Elena Gomez: action — who owns the benchmark run and data transfer?
[31:05] Liam O'Neill: Redwood SE (that's me) will run the bench; we'll ask for an s3 link or sanitized sample data; we'll handle it under NDA.

[32:20] Ravi Patel: any known competitor pitfalls? we were also talking to a few vendors.
[32:27] Maya Chen: some competitors lock you into a single model stack or don't offer dedicated/private parity. others don't have deep runtime optimizations for long context which affects cost and latency. will include a short competitor note in the follow-up.

[33:55] Sophie Martin: ok let's recap and assign next steps.
[34:00] Maya Chen: recap — Redwood to run 8k & 32k benchmarks on three models with your eval set (SE: Liam). Redwood to share pricing template for hosted/dedicated/private (AE: Maya). Redwood to share security pack (AE: Maya). Schedule a deep-dive demo of Dedicated network setup and tooling (AE + SE).

[35:10] Ravi Patel: timeline: we'll aim for the benchmark results by 11/10 so we can decide before end of month.
[35:18] Maya Chen: sounds doable — we'll target 11/10.

[36:30] Elena Gomez: small nit: do you have pre-built pipelines for multilingual QA?
[36:36] Liam O'Neill: we have templates and RAG patterns that are language-agnostic; recommend language-specific tokenizers and eval to tune prompts per language.

[38:00] Sophie Martin: any docs on function calling best practices?
[38:05] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include a short best-practices doc and an example using a retrieval + tool-calling flow.

[39:25] Ravi Patel: final Q — can Dedicated be bursty? we have seasonal spikes.
[39:32] Maya Chen: yes — Dedicated has autoscaling policies and burst capacity options so you can have base reserved and burst to shared pool.

[41:00] Elena Gomez: thanks everyone.
[41:05] Maya Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with the benchmark plan and docs.
[41:10] Liam O'Neill: I'll send a short questionnaire for the sample dataset and the benchmark rubric.
[41:20] Sophie Martin: perfect.

[46:50] (call end)

Notes: transcript contains occasional small transcription errors and speaker overlaps; this file is an export of the Fireflies.ai call artifact.
